page: Amazon Web Services c8i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, the instance delivers 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core. The processor features a large 480 MB L3 cache and supports modern vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity is configured at 32 GB of DDR5 operating at 7 GHz, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware configurations exclude local instance storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. Baseline networking throughput is rated at 8 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. In benchmark testing, the instance shows notable single-core throughput, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2211.0 and top-decile text processing throughput of 2952.0. Single-threaded data compression also ranks in the top quartile, registering 34.45 GB/sec in gzip compression and 14.45 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression.

Instruction set extensions such as AMX enable competitive CPU-based machine learning inference, demonstrated by a top-tier result of 348.03 tokens per second in small model text generation. Multi-core performance metrics, such as PassMark CPU (29,107.56) and stress-ng multi-core (17,296.91), align with standard expectations for 16-vCPU hardware. Without bundled ephemeral NVMe storage, the server requires reliance on Amazon EBS, presenting an I/O tradeoff for storage-heavy tasks. The c8i.4xlarge is functionally suited for compute-bound workloads, batch processing, CI/CD build runners, web serving, and lightweight AI inferencing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i.4xlarge is a compute-optimized Nitro-based virtual server powered by a 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor on x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 32 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory (2 GB per vCPU), and 480 MB of shared L3 cache. Acceleration features include AVX-512 and Intel AMX, while dedicated GPUs and local storage are absent, routing disk operations through network storage over an 8 Gbps baseline network. Synthetic benchmarks show strong single-core performance, highlighted by top-quartile Geekbench single-thread execution and superior small-model LLM generation speeds. Given its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and high clock speed, the instance is structurally aligned with compute-intensive tasks, code compilation, automated CI/CD pipelines, and web serving.
